docRequirement: auto-mode-config.md binds the literal string "$defaults" inside an `autoMode` array to a splice of the classifier's built-in rule list for that section: "To keep the built-in rules while adding your own, include the literal string `"$defaults"` in the array. The default rules are spliced in at that position, so your custom rules can go before or after them" (:182, and the same sentence for `environment` at :103). The Danger callout at :212 binds the inverse: "Setting any of `environment`, `allow`, `soft_deny`, or `hard_deny` without `"$defaults"` replaces the entire default list for that section", naming the built-in soft blocks (force push, `curl | bash`, production deploys, auto-mode bypass) and the built-in `hard_deny` data-exfiltration rule as what is discarded. :218 adds that each of the four sections is evaluated independently.
current: The sentinel is a recognised constant and the splice primitive is correct, but nothing is ever spliced. `AUTO_MODE_DEFAULTS_SENTINEL = '$defaults'` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:478) is consumed by `resolveAutoModeList` (:1061-1067), which flatMaps the sentinel to `[...defaults]` and returns `[...defaults]` for an absent list. `resolveAutoMode` (:1082-1101) declares `defaults: Partial<ResolvedAutoModePolicyV1> = {}` (:1089) and composes `resolveAutoModeList(scopes.managed?.[key], defaults[key] ?? [])` plus `resolveAutoModeList(scopes.user?.[key], [])` (:1092-1093). The ONLY production caller is packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4109, `resolveAutoMode({ managed: this.managedPiPolicy.autoMode })` — no second argument — so every `defaults[key]` is `[]` and the sentinel resolves to nothing. Live probe against the real modules: `resolveAutoMode({ managed: { soft_deny: ['$defaults','no hand migrations'] } })` and `resolveAutoMode({ managed: { soft_deny: ['no hand migrations'] } })` both return `{environment:[],hard_deny:[],soft_deny:['no hand migrations'],allow:[]}`, and `buildGuardianJudgeTask` produces a byte-identical task for the two (`task identical true`); the primitive itself works — `resolveAutoModeList(['a','$defaults','b'], ['D1'])` returns `['a','D1','b']`. The shipped test already pins the broken shape at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.test.ts:1025. No built-in rule list exists as data anywhere: an exhaustive `grep -a` for `soft_deny` over packages/apps/scripts/docs finds only the type declarations (managed-policy.ts:437, :464, guardian.ts:260), the parser (:850), the composer (:1098), the renderer (guardian.ts:346) and tests. Our built-in rules live instead as unconditional prose inside the judge's system prompt — `GUARDIAN_POLICY_PROMPT` sections `## Data Exfiltration` / `## Credential Probing` / `## Persistent Security Weakening` / `## Destructive Actions` (packages/shared/src/prompts/guardian.ts:153-173) — installed as `systemPrompt: GUARDIAN_POLICY_PROMPT` at packages/shared/src/agent/core/guardian-judge-core.ts:110 on every judge run, while the managed block only APPENDS a `## Organization policy` section to the task (guardian.ts:372, :382-383) and `describeOrgPolicy` returns `null` when all four resolved sets are empty (:342-349). The resolved value reaches the judge through the in-process `SessionCapabilityTurnRuntime.managedAutoMode` field (packages/shared/src/agent/backend/types.ts:610), read at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:3350-3353 where `hasAutoModePolicy` (managed-policy.ts:1110) drops it when every set is empty, and consumed at the two consult sites pi-agent.ts:3412/:3421 and :3516/:3527.
divergence: Not a key-name or value error: the sentinel string, the splice position semantics and the replace-on-absence semantics are all implemented correctly in `resolveAutoModeList`. What is missing is the operand — there are no built-in `environment`/`hard_deny`/`soft_deny`/`allow` lists in this fork to splice, and the sole production call site passes no `defaults`. Consequence in both documented directions: (1) including `"$defaults"` splices nothing, so a managed `['$defaults','x']` and a managed `['x']` produce byte-identical judge input, and the sentinel is silently swallowed with no drop record and no diagnostic; (2) omitting `"$defaults"` discards nothing, because the built-in taxonomy is unconditional prose in the judge's system prompt rather than one of the four addressable lists, so the Danger case at :212 is unreachable. The fork is therefore fail-safe on enforcement (no built-in protection is ever lost) and wrong on configuration (the documented splice is a no-op, and the documented take-full-ownership escape hatch does not exist).

userImpact: For the documented add-your-own-rules case: none observable. An administrator who ships the page's example (`"soft_deny": ["$defaults", "Never run migrations outside the migrations CLI"]`) in the host-owned managed policy gets exactly the guardian behaviour they would get without the sentinel — verified by probe, the two produce a byte-identical judge task — and no protection is lost, because the built-in taxonomy is in the judge's system prompt regardless. The sentinel is dropped silently: the parser accepts it as ordinary prose (managed-policy.ts:837-847 records no drop), and there is no `claude auto-mode config`/`defaults` equivalent to inspect the effective list, so the admin has no surface that would reveal it. What IS observable is the take-full-ownership case the Danger callout describes: an admin who deliberately omits `"$defaults"` to drop a built-in rule — e.g. a team that force-pushes feature branches routinely and wants the built-in destructive-git soft block gone — still gets it applied, so in `auto` mode those pushes keep being routed to a human prompt with a guardian objection, and the only workaround is to add a counter-entry to `allow`. Latent today because the fork has no delivered managed policies in the wild that use the sentinel; it surfaces the moment one does.
